info.name: BPMSquare · Workforce Management (WFM) API
info.description:
Complete WFM API surface for QA — functional, negative and stress testing.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SETUP (do this once)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Import the companion environment file and fill in:
     baseUrl            https://<tenant-host>            <- tenant is resolved FROM THE HOSTNAME
     supabaseUrl        https://<project>.supabase.co
     supabaseAnonKey    the public anon key
     employeeEmail / employeePassword
     supervisorEmail / supervisorPassword
     adminEmail / adminPassword
     otherEmployeeId    a second employee's UUID (for the cross-user 403 cases)
     cronSecret         only if testing 11.x

2. Run "0.x · Sign in" for the persona you want, then ALWAYS run "0.4 · Establish app session".
   Confirm with "0.5 · Who am I".

⚠ TENANT IS RESOLVED FROM THE HOSTNAME, not from a header or a body field. Testing a different
tenant means changing baseUrl to that tenant's host — there is no tenant switch, and no request
field will ever override it. Any endpoint that appears to accept a tenant id is a bug worth
reporting immediately.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
THE THREE PERSONAS — this drives most of the test matrix
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
EMPLOYEE    punches, sees ONLY their own data, files corrections/leave, responds to rechecks.
SUPERVISOR  everything above + the live board, everyone's presence, the monthly summary, and
            approval of OT / corrections / leave. (employees.wfm_role = 'supervisor', OR a tenant
            admin, OR granted via a Business Role.)
ADMIN       everything above + configuration: shifts, sites, holidays, leave types, and
            Settings -> Workforce. A supervisor who is NOT an admin gets 403 on all of those.

Folder 12 exists to prove those boundaries hold server-side. Each request there says which
persona to be signed in as — the UI hides these actions, so the API is the real gate.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SUGGESTED RUN ORDER
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
0 (admin) -> 9 (create shift/site/leave type) -> 0 (employee) -> 1 (punch cycle incl. OT)
  -> 2 -> 4/5 (file) -> 0 (supervisor) -> 3/4/5 (approve) -> 6/7/8/10 -> 12 (negatives)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
STRESS TESTING — where the load actually lands
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Read-heavy, in descending cost:
  GET /api/wfm/summary?month=      recomputes EVERY employee's month. The heaviest call.
  GET /api/wfm/summary/export      same, plus xlsx generation. Heaviest response body.
  GET /api/wfm/live-board          polled ~every 30s per open supervisor screen — the highest
                                   sustained request rate in normal use.
  GET /api/wfm/presence            first call per employee-day is slower: it mints signed selfie
                                   URLs and lazily reverse-geocodes. Measure cold AND warm.
  GET /api/wfm/me/timesheet        per-employee month; the fan-out case is many employees at once.

Write-heavy:
  POST /api/wfm/punch              the burst case is real: a whole shift punching in within a few
                                   minutes of each other. Each punch does a state read, a config
                                   read, an insert, and a running-total recompute.
  POST /api/wfm/roster             up to 3000 upserted rows in ONE call.
  PATCH /api/wfm/employees/bulk-*  up to 500 rows per call.

Concurrency cases worth deliberately racing:
  * Two punches for the SAME employee submitted simultaneously — state is read then written, so
    this is the interesting race. Correct behaviour: one succeeds, the other 409s or is absorbed
    as a duplicate. Two events that both land would be a real finding.
  * The same punch id replayed N times in parallel (offline sync) — must yield exactly one event.
  * Two supervisors approving the SAME OT session at once — exactly one should win, the other 409.

Tooling: `newman run` for functional regression; k6/JMeter for load. For load, sign in ONCE and
reuse the cookie rather than re-authenticating per virtual user — Supabase Auth applies its own
project-level rate limits and you will measure those instead of the app.

Note: the app has NO application-level rate limiting on these routes. If a test saturates it,
that is a capacity finding, not a bug — report the numbers rather than a pass/fail.

item.name: 1 · Punch (employee)
item.description: The write path: consent, the full punch cycle, OT, mobile work, business trip, and the selfie attachment.

request.description: Punching is blocked with 403 until this is stamped. Set-once and idempotent.

Records ONE presence event. The write path everything else in WFM hangs off.

Rules the server enforces (all return an error, never a silent accept):
* `id` MUST be a client-generated UUID. Re-sending the same id is an idempotent no-op
  (`{ok:true, duplicate:true}`) — that is how the offline queue retries safely.
* `kind` must be legal FROM THE CURRENT STATE. State machine:
    out   -> check_in | mobile_work_start | business_trip_start | ot_in
    in    -> break_start | check_out | mobile_work_end | business_trip_end
    break -> break_end | check_out | mobile_work_end | business_trip_end
    ot    -> ot_out
  Anything else is 409. Note there is NO path from `in`/`break` into `ot` — that is the
  structural implementation of the client's "no OT between check-in and check-out".
* `ts` is optional (defaults to now). Accepted window: 7 days in the past, 5 minutes in
  the future. It must also be strictly LATER than your previous punch.
* `geo` is optional. Whether being outside a geofence blocks the punch depends on
  Settings -> Workforce -> geofence_mode (block / flag / off).
* Optional punch types (ot, mobile_work, business_trip) 403 unless enabled for the tenant.
kind = break_start
kind = break_end
Closes the working session. Must happen BEFORE any OT punch — the client's rule.
Only legal from state `out`. Requires punch_types.ot enabled (else 403).

item.name: 3 · Overtime
item.description: OT sessions are created automatically by an ot_out punch and stay PENDING until a supervisor approves. Only approved OT reaches pay.

query.description: supervisor only; ignored for an employee

request.description: Supervisor sees the whole tenant queue (with employee names joined); a plain employee sees only their own rows — the employee_id param is ignored for them, not honoured.
THE PAY GATE. Only approved sessions count toward ot_minutes / ot_amount in the monthly summary and the CA export. Already-resolved sessions return 409 (no double-approve).
supervisor_remark is MANDATORY on reject (400 without it) and optional on approve.

item.name: 4 · Corrections (employee files, supervisor approves)
item.description: Append-only: approving inserts a new event and supersedes the old one.

request.description: Supervisor sees the tenant queue; an employee sees only their own.

issue ∈ missing_check_in | missing_check_out | wrong_time | other.
proposed_ts is REQUIRED for missing_check_in / missing_check_out.
This NEVER edits attendance — filing a request changes nothing until a supervisor approves.

item.name: 4.3 · File a correction — wrong time on a specific punch

request.description: target_event_id is verified to belong to the caller — someone else's event id returns 400.
Append-only by design: approval INSERTS a new source='correction' event and stamps superseded_by on the old one. The original row is never edited or deleted.
supervisor_remark mandatory on reject.

item.name: 5 · Leave
item.description: Request/approve flow, plus the supervisor's direct-entry ledger.

request.description: Supervisor sees the tenant queue; an employee sees only their own.
leave_type_id must be an ACTIVE type in this tenant (400 otherwise). date_to < date_from is 400. half_day is only meaningful when from == to. Writes nothing to wfm_leave_records — approval does that.
Approval INSERTS a wfm_leave_records row — that record, not the request, is what moves the leave balance and the monthly summary.
supervisor_remark mandatory.
The approved/absolute leave ledger, supervisor-only.
Supervisor records leave without a request/approval round-trip. Both employee_id and leave_type_id are tenant-verified before the insert.
Supervisor only.
The reverse direction of a correction: a supervisor flags a punch and the employee answers.
recheck_type ∈ time | selfie | both (defaults to both). Omit target_event_id to flag the whole day. Both employee_id and target_event_id are tenant-verified.

item.name: 7 · Roster
item.description: Date-range reads and bulk assignment with hard server-side caps.

request.description: A plain employee ALWAYS gets only their own rows regardless of employee_id.

Upserts on (tenant, employee, date) — re-assigning a date overwrites it.
Caps QA should push against: 500 employees, 62 dates, and 3000 employee×date combinations per call. shift_id is required unless is_day_off is true. Every employee id must resolve inside the tenant or the WHOLE call 400s (deliberately loud, not a partial apply).
Reverts that employee/date to their standing shift.

item.name: 8 · Employees (supervisor/admin)
item.description: Master data, the employee hub, login provisioning and bulk assignment.

request.description: WFM fields + shift/site names + login status.
Identity, site/shift/supervisor, direct reports, month totals, leave balance.
employment_type is validated against the TENANT's configured list (Settings -> Workforce), not a hardcoded enum. Duplicate employee_code returns 409.
Every foreign id (shift, site, supervisor) is tenant-verified. Self-supervision is explicitly rejected. Send null to clear a link.

Admin-set initial password (no magic link / email confirmation by product decision). Password must be ≥8 chars. 409 if the employee already has a login, or if that login is already bound to a different employee. The user is forced to change it at first sign-in.
Max 500 ids. Pass shift_id: null to clear. Any id outside the tenant 400s the whole call.
Same shape and caps as bulk-shift.

request.description: 403 if the tenant doesn't have the wfm feature flag.

Partial merge — only recognised, well-typed keys are applied; anything invalid is silently ignored rather than 400ing, so QA must GET after PUT to confirm what actually landed.
Notable validation: employment_type CODES must match ^[a-z0-9_]{1,40}$, the list can never be saved empty, codes are de-duplicated, and a code must never be renamed once employees reference it. geofence_mode ∈ block|flag|off. ot_rate_per_hour must be a finite number ≥ 0.

item.name: 10 · Supervisor views
item.description: Live board, presence audit, monthly summary and the Excel export — the main read-load targets.

request.description: Today's attendance for every employee: state, first-in/last-out, late/absent, geofence flags. The UI polls this about every 30s — the main sustained-read target for stress testing.

The audit view. Mints a 5-minute signed URL per selfie (private bucket) and lazily reverse-geocodes any punch that has coordinates but no cached address — so the FIRST call for a given day is materially slower than repeats. Worth measuring both.
Access: your own always; anyone else's only as supervisor (403 otherwise).
The CA-facing monthly aggregate incl. OT minutes and OT amount. Heaviest read in the module — it recomputes every employee's month. Primary stress-test target.
Returns an .xlsx binary, one sheet per configured employment type plus an 'Other' catch-all. Heaviest single response in WFM.

Supervisor+. Proxies an external maps provider server-side so the API key never reaches the client. 404 when nothing matches, 503 when the provider is unavailable — QA should treat 503 as a provider issue, not an app bug.

Daily Vercel cron. Purges punch SELFIES older than the tenant's selfie_retention_days — the presence events themselves are kept forever, and enrollment photos are NOT touched. Runs across every wfm-enabled tenant. Authenticated by the CRON_SECRET bearer, not a session.
Negative control for the only unauthenticated-by-session route in WFM.

exec: // No bearer token — must never execute a purge.
